pull.title: KAFKA-21356: Relieve the persister thread of share group DLQ processing.
pull.body:
Copying records into the DLQ was dominated by work on the persister
thread, which also completes write responses for every share partition:

- isDlqEnabledOnTopic and dlqTopicMaxMessageBytes built a LogConfig,
which parses every topic config, on each DLQ request. Read the one key
directly. (Affects both copy on and off case)
- The source record read of ran synchronously on the persister thread.
Run it (and later rounds) on a single-threaded fetch executor owned and
shut down by BrokerServer. (Affects copy on case)
- ShareGroupDLQRecordFetcher.collectRecords visited every batch of a 1
MiB log read, loading each file-backed batch from disk, although a
request wants a few records. We can simply reject batches where the
batch baseOffset > dlq endoffset (V2 only, Affects copy on case).
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Reviewers: Andrew Schofield <aschofield@confluent.io>

repo.name: kafka
repo.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

reviews.body: Thanks for the updates. A few more comments.

review_comments.body: The "Constructing a LogConfig...." sentence is justification for the PR, rather than a useful thing to have in a comment.

review_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -943,6 +957,15 @@ class BrokerServer(
       if (shareGroupDLQManager != null)
         Utils.swallow(this.logger.underlying, () => shareGroupDLQManager.stop())
 
+      // Stopped after the DLQ manager so that nothing submits to it any more. Reads still running or
+      // queued are given a moment to finish and are interrupted otherwise.
+      if (shareGroupDLQFetchExecutor != null)
+        Utils.swallow(this.logger.underlying, () => {
+          shareGroupDLQFetchExecutor.shutdown()
review_comments.body: Doesn't this use ReplicaManager? Is the shutdown order sensible?
This comment is misleading now I think.
Won't that already be true because of the configuration validation for the topic?
Using a daemon thread is an improvement. Would a small number of threads be better than just one?

review_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -178,6 +178,9 @@ class BrokerServer(
 
   private var shareGroupDLQManager: ShareGroupDLQManager = _
 
+  // Runs the source record reads of the share group DLQ manager, off the persister thread.
+  private var shareGroupDLQFetchExecutor: ExecutorService = _
review_comments.body: I wonder whether the ExecutorService ought to be within the DLQ manager.
will add a new internal config for this.
This can't be null. If it's bad, you're going to end up with an exception instead.
You will need to apply bounds checking to the returned value though I think.

This just orphans enqueued but unstarted tasks without completing their futures. You should capture the return value from `fetchExecutor.shutdownNow()` and process the list of tasks to fail their futures.

commit.message:
KAFKA-21356: Relieve the persister thread of share group DLQ record copy work

Copying records into the DLQ was dominated by work on the persister thread,
which also completes write responses for every share partition:

- isDlqEnabledOnTopic and dlqTopicMaxMessageBytes built a LogConfig, which
  parses every topic config, on each DLQ request. Read the one key directly.
- The source record read of round 1 ran synchronously on the persister thread.
  Run it (and later rounds) on a single-threaded fetch executor owned and shut
  down by BrokerServer.
- ShareGroupDLQRecordFetcher.collectRecords visited every batch of a 1 MiB log
  read, loading each file-backed batch from disk, although a request wants a
  few records. For v2 batches stop at the first batch starting after the end
  offset and skip batches ending before the read position. Legacy batches are
  still always visited.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

KAFKA-21356: Skip batches beyond the DLQ range without relying on batch order

collectRecords stopped at the first v2 batch starting beyond the end offset of
the range. That depends on the batches of a read being returned in offset
order. Look at every batch instead and skip, with a continue, each v2 batch
whose base offset is beyond the end offset. The check reads nothing beyond what
finding the batch already read, and a skipped batch's body is never loaded.

Drop the check for batches ending before the read position: a read starts at
the batch containing the read position, and records below it are already
skipped record by record.

Legacy (v0/v1) batches are still always visited, as their baseOffset() loads
and, if compressed, decompresses the batch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

KAFKA-21356: Address review comments on the share group DLQ fetch executor

- Move the record fetch executor into DefaultShareGroupDLQManager, which now
  creates it and drains it in stop(). The pool size is set by the new internal
  config group.share.dlq.manager.fetcher.num.threads (default 2).
- Stop the share partition manager, persister and DLQ manager before the share
  coordinator and the replica manager, which they depend on.
- Reword the comments about LogConfig and the DLQ record resolution, and drop
  the redundant message.max.bytes lower bound check.
- Add tests for the executor ownership and shutdown, off-caller record reads,
  a rejecting executor and the new config.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

KAFKA-21356: Address second round of review comments on the DLQ fetch executor

- Apply the topic config bounds to a topic-level max.message.bytes override
  when sizing DLQ records, using the validator from LogConfig, and drop the
  null check that can never be hit.
- Shut the fetch executor down with shutdown() and awaitTermination() only.
  shutdownNow() is avoided as it would interrupt threads which may be reading
  a log segment, closing the segment's FileChannel for its other users.
- Correct the comments which still said source records are read on the
  calling thread.
- Add tests for the max.message.bytes bounds and for stop() running queued
  reads without interrupting running ones.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

       if (partitionMetadataClient != null)
         Utils.swallow(this.logger.underlying, () => partitionMetadataClient.close())
 
+      Utils.closeQuietly(sharePartitionManager, "share partition manager")
+
+      // The order of closing sharePartitionManager, groupCoordinator and persister matters.
+      // groupCoordinator, sharePartitionManager must be closed before the persister so that
+      // new requests from sharePartitionManager, groupCoordinator do not encounter a stopped
+      // persister.
+      if (persister != null)
+        Utils.swallow(this.logger.underlying, () => persister.stop())
+
+      // The order of closing sharePartitionManager and shareGroupDLQManager matters.
+      // sharePartitionManager must be closed before the shareGroupDLQManager so any new
+      // requests from sharePartitionManager do not encounter a stopped shareGroupDLQManager.
+      // They are also closed before the shareCoordinator and the replicaManager, which the persister
+      // and the DLQ manager's reads of source records depend on.
+      if (shareGroupDLQManager != null)
+        Utils.swallow(this.logger.underlying, () => shareGroupDLQManager.stop())
+
       if (shareCoordinator != null)
         Utils.swallow(this.logger.underlying, () => shareCoordinator.shutdown())
